1) 先确认是否是计划内变更；2) 非计划则执行 journalctl -u s: 1) First confirm whether this was a planned change; 2) If unplanned, run journalctl -u slapd --since '-30min' to find the cause; 3) Run dmesg -T | grep -i 'killed process' to check for an OOM kill; an oversized olcDbMaxSize on the mdb backend is a common trigger; 4) After the restart verify service with ldapsearch -x -b '' -s base namingContexts and confirm replicas have caught up.
1) 执行 ldapsearch -x -D \u003cbind_dn\u00: 1) Run ldapsearch -x -D <bind_dn> -w <pw> -b 'cn=Connections,cn=Monitor' to list current connections and find the client IP holding the most; 2) Many connections from a single application means it is not reusing or closing connections; push the application team to use a connection pool; 3) As a stopgap raise slapd's ulimit -n (LimitNOFILE under systemd) and restart; 4) Also check whether olcIdleTimeout is configured, since without it idle connections hold descriptors forever.

1) Run ldapsearch -x -D <bind_dn> -w <pw> -b 'cn=Operations,cn=Monitor' and compare Initiated with Completed per operation type to find where things are stuck; 2) If Modify/Add are stuck, check backend database locks and disk IO (iostat -x 1); the mdb backend blocks easily under write amplification; 3) If Search is stuck, follow the slow-query path and add indexes; 4) If replication (syncrepl) is holding the provider back, check the connectivity and lag of each consumer and detach a broken consumer if necessary.

1) Run ldapsearch -x -D <bind_dn> -w <pw> -b 'cn=Operations,cn=Monitor' to see which operation type (Search/Bind/Modify) dominates; 2) When Search dominates, hunt slow queries: enable loglevel stats in slapd.conf and find the SRCH filters with high duration in the log, then index the matching attributes (olcDbIndex); 3) After adding indexes rebuild them with slapindex (slapd must be stopped first); 4) If indexing is not the problem, raise olcThreads (default 16) and check whether CPU core count has become the bottleneck.

1) Run ldapsearch -x -D <bind_dn> -w <pw> -b 'cn=Threads,cn=Monitor' to see the live Active and Max values; 2) Enable stats logging to locate slow operations, paying particular attention to unindexed substring filters such as (cn=*abc*) that force a full scan; 3) Add olcDbIndex for the frequently filtered attributes and rebuild with slapindex; this is the most effective way to shed load; 4) If indexing is already complete and it is still saturated, raise olcThreads or add read-only replicas (syncrepl consumers) to offload queries.
OpenLDAP 操作完成数落后于发起数: OpenLDAP completed operations lagging behind initiated
OpenLDAP 连接数逼近文件描述符上限: OpenLDAP connections approaching the file descriptor limit
slapd 线程池中有请求在排队等待线程，说明工作线程已全部占满，LDAP 查询: Requests are queued waiting for a thread in the slapd thread pool, meaning all worker threads are busy. LDAP query latency will rise noticeably.
slapd 运行时间不足 5 分钟，说明刚重启过；若不是计划内操作，可能是崩溃、: slapd has been running for less than 5 minutes, so it restarted recently. If this was not planned it may be a crash, an OOM kill, or a failed configuration reload.
已发起但未完成的 LDAP 操作累计超过 100 个，说明有操作长时间阻塞未返回: More than 100 LDAP operations have been initiated but not completed, meaning some operations are blocked and never returning. Clients experience hung requests.
当前连接数已占到 slapd 可用文件描述符上限的 80%，打满后新的 LDAP: Current connections have reached 80% of slapd's usable file descriptor limit. Once it is exhausted new LDAP bind requests fail outright, and every system that relies on LDAP for authentication will fail to log in.
活跃工作线程已占到线程池上限的 90%，再涨请求就会开始排队，属于线程池打满的前: Active worker threads have reached 90% of the thread pool limit. Any further growth means requests start queuing; this is the precursor to a saturated pool.
